title.narrative: Promoting sustainable fisheries management in the Red Sea Large Marine Ecosystem (RedSeaFish project)

description.narrative: 177. The RedSeaFish project will deliver significant socio-economic benefits at both regional and local levels, contributing long-lasting impacts on the livelihoods of fishing communities and across the Red Sea region. By strengthening regional cooperation (Component 2) and measures to promote sustainable fisheries management at both national and regional levels (Component 1,2 and 3), the project will help stabilize fish stocks and in the longer-term help reverse declines, ensuring the long-term viability of the fishing industry and providing economic stability for coastal communities that rely on fisheries as their primary livelihood source. With better fish stock assessment and management (Component 1), fishing communities will experience more consistent and sustainable harvests, improving their financial and food security and reducing the pressures of overfishing. The project’s focus on improving fisheries data collection and management systems and involving them in data collection and decision-making (under Component 1) will give communities and stakeholders reliable information for decision-making which will support the development of better policies tailored to local needs. In addition, the project has a specific element on strengthening systems for co-management of fisheries (under Component 3), particularly empowering fisher communities, not just national fisheries agencies, to be able to effectively participate in fisheries management decision-making. In addition, Component 4 through which the project’s knowledge management and learning activities will be coordinated, will provide important capacity through awareness-raising and outreach activities, improving knowledge for enabling action, directed at both national fisheries agencies and local fisher communities on responsible fishing practices.178. A key focus of the project is on gender equality and ensuring women can participate equally and have opportunities to benefit from the project. The project will support and promote women’s involvement in fisheries management, from data collection to decision-making, through providing resources, training, and leadership opportunities. By addressing gender gaps, the project will create more inclusive and equitable outcomes, benefiting both men and women in the sector and fostering a more balanced approach to resource management.179. The development of a regional working group and Regional Fisheries Management Plans (RFMPs) will harmonize fisheries management practices across Red Sea countries, ensuring that fisheries resources are shared equitably and managed sustainably. This regional approach will help reduce conflicts over resources and promote cooperation and build trust between neighboring countries. As a result, fishing communities will benefit from more stable incomes, improved market access, and a more predictable regulatory environment that supports sustainable practices.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
To strengthen regional cooperation and management for sustainable shared fisheries in the Red Sea.
